container: The digital divide refers to the gap between those who have ready access to computers and the internet and those who do not. This disparity affects education, employment, healthcare, and social connectivity. In many rural and low-income communities, limited infrastructure and affordability prevent individuals from accessing essential digital tools. Without reliable internet, students struggle to complete online assignments, job seekers miss out on remote opportunities, and patients cannot use telehealth services. Governments and organizations must invest in broadband expansion, provide affordable devices, and offer digital literacy training. Bridging the digital divide is crucial for promoting equality and ensuring that everyone can participate fully in the modern world. Closing this gap supports economic growth, educational advancement, and social inclusion for all, regardless of background or location.
